passages.t: Gods that must be carried, and a God who carries
passages.happening:
‘Bel crouches; Nebo cowers. Their idols weigh down beasts and cattle’ (verse 1). The images are a heavy load on weary animals. The gods cannot relieve the burden; they themselves go into captivity (verse 2).

‘Listen to Me, O house of Jacob, all the remnant of the house of Israel, who have been sustained from the womb, carried along since birth’ (verse 3). ‘Even to your old age, I will be the same, and I will bear you up when you turn gray. I have made you, and I will carry you; I will sustain you and deliver you’ (verse 4).

To whom will they compare him (verse 5)? People pour gold from their bags and weigh silver, hire a goldsmith to make a god, and bow down (verse 6). ‘They lift it to their shoulder and carry it along’ (verse 7), set it in its place, and there it stands, unable to move. They cry to it, and it does not answer or save anyone.
passages.hearers:
Bel was a title meaning lord, used in this period for Marduk, the patron god of Babylon and head of its gods. Nebo is Nabu, Marduk's son, god of writing and wisdom. The kings of Babylon bore names honoring them: Nebuchadnezzar and Nabonidus contain the name of Nabu, and Belshazzar contains Bel. Each spring at the New Year festival, Nabu's statue was brought to Babylon and the images of the gods were carried in great processions.

The picture here turns the procession into a retreat. The great gods are loaded onto tired animals and hauled away, too heavy to carry themselves. As Cyrus approached in 539 BC, Babylonian records say that Nabonidus brought gods from other cities into Babylon, and after his victory Cyrus sent them back. Cyrus himself honored Marduk rather than carrying him off, so the picture is best read as a poetic picture of the gods' helplessness, not a report of one event.

The contrast is the point of the chapter. Babylon's gods have to be carried. Israel's God carries his people, from the womb to gray hair.
passages.later: Moses told Israel how ‘the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way by which you traveled’ (Deuteronomy 1:31). A psalm mocks idols that ‘have mouths, but cannot speak’ (Psalm 115:5).
passages.asks: Babylon's gods had to be carried; Israel's God carries his people. Ask what you are carrying that you thought would carry you. And ask whether you believe God will still carry you when you turn gray.

passages.t: The end declared from the beginning
passages.happening:
‘Remember this and be brave; take it to heart, you transgressors’ (verse 8). Remember what happened long ago: ‘for I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is none like Me’ (verse 9).

‘I declare the end from the beginning, and ancient times from what is still to come’ (verse 10). God's purpose will stand, and he will do all he pleases (verse 10). ‘I summon a bird of prey from the east, a man for My purpose from a far-off land’ (verse 11). He has spoken and will bring it about.

‘Listen to Me, you stubborn people, far removed from righteousness’ (verse 12). ‘I am bringing My righteousness near; it is not far away, and My salvation will not be delayed. I will grant salvation to Zion and adorn Israel with My splendor’ (verse 13).
passages.hearers:
The bird of prey from the east is Cyrus, swooping down on Babylon.

God speaks to stubborn people, far from righteousness, and promises to bring his righteousness near. It does not wait for them to deserve it. Righteousness here is God's saving faithfulness, the right he does in rescuing his people.

The first hearers were told that God's plan was not a guess. He announced the end from the beginning, and the coming of Cyrus would prove it.
passages.later: Paul writes that ‘the righteousness of God has been revealed’ (Romans 3:21). And a psalm says, ‘The counsel of the LORD stands forever’ (Psalm 33:11).
passages.asks: God brings his righteousness near to stubborn people. Ask whether you think you have to become righteous before God will come near. And ask what it would mean to remember the things God did long ago in your own life.
